title: Biftekia
subtitle: Greek herbed beef and lamb burgers cooked on the griddle
excerpt: Thick, juicy Greek patties made from a mix of minced beef and lamb with onion, parsley and oregano. Cooked on a hot griddle until well charred outside and just pink inside. Serve with lemon wedges.
sourceNotes: Greek taverna and home kitchen staple; cooked over charcoal in summer, on a griddle pan year round.

recipe.freezeNotes: Freeze the raw shaped patties on a tray, then bag up. Cook from frozen, adding 5 minutes to each side.
recipe.batchNotes: Scale up with no changes. Shape and chill in advance, then cook in batches.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Shape the patties up to 24 hours ahead. Keep on a plate, covered, in the fridge.

content.text: Biftekia are Greek patties made from a blend of minced beef and lamb, seasoned generously with herbs. Chilling them before cooking helps them hold together on the griddle. Press them no thicker than 2cm or the outside will char before the centre cooks through.
Combine both minces, the grated onion, garlic, parsley, oregano, breadcrumbs, beaten egg, salt and pepper in a bowl. Mix thoroughly with your hands.
Divide the mixture into 8 equal portions. Shape each into a flat oval patty about 2cm thick.
Place on a plate, cover and refrigerate for 30 minutes. This helps them firm up and hold together on the griddle.
Heat a griddle pan over a high heat until very hot. Brush with olive oil just before cooking.
Cook the patties for 5 to 6 minutes on the first side without moving them. Turn and cook for 4 to 5 minutes more.
Rest on a warm plate for 5 minutes. Serve with lemon wedges.

items.symptom: The patties break apart on the griddle.
items.cause: The mixture was not chilled, or the onion was too wet.
items.fix: Squeeze the grated onion in a clean cloth to remove excess liquid before adding it to the mix.

items.symptom: The outside chars before the centre is cooked.
items.cause: The patties were too thick, or the heat was too high.
items.fix: Press to 2cm thickness maximum. Reduce the heat to medium-high and cook for longer if needed.

items.cause: The pan was not hot enough before the oil went in, or the patties were moved too soon.
items.fix: Heat the pan fully before oiling. Leave the patties untouched for the full 5 minutes so they release naturally.
